articles.title: ‘I just wasn’t going to give up’: the fight to free the longest-serving political prisoner in the US
articles.summary: Leonard Peltier was imprisoned for 49 years before his sentence was commuted. A new Netflix documentary exposes the ‘corrupt’ system that allowed it to happen. On 20 January 2025, with 14 minutes remaining in his term as president, Joe Biden commuted the life sentence of Leonard Peltier, after…
body: Outside the Florida prison where Peltier was being held that morning were several of the many activists and lawyers who fought for his release, as well as film-makers David France and Jesse Short Bull. The two directors’ long-gestating documentary on Peltier’s fight for justice was set to premiere just a week later at the Sundance film festival with a very different ending, the octogenarian still awaiting a chance to return home to the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa reservation in North Dakota. That morning, there was “a sinking feeling that it wasn’t going to happen”, France said.

When it did, while the cameras rolled, the line of supporters erupted in joy for a commutation that allowed Peltier to serve the rest of his consecutive life sentences on house arrest, though it did not pardon him – not quite justice, but a victory so uncertain and so hard-fought, over more than half a lifetime, that I have cried every time I’ve rewatched it.

articles.title: AI Can Cut Film Budgets by Up to 40%, Says ‘The Outlaws’ Director Kang Yoon-sung, as Netflix Reveals Use on 300 Titles: ‘A Human Touch Is Absolutely Essential’
articles.summary: Netflix has used AI in one form or another on some 300 of its titles, Lee Sung-gyun, the streamer’s senior director of APAC production, told an audience at the Busan International Film Festival.
body: On the same panel, “The Outlaws” director Kang Yoon-sung said AI workflows could take 30% to 40% off a feature film’s production budget.

Lee said new technology has always startled people when it arrives. “All these technological changes and new tools have helped a great deal with the ‘how,’ how we make what we make better, but they never decided the ‘why,’ why we have to tell this story,” he said. “AI is the same.”

He also screened a reel from Eyeline, Netflix’s VFX studio, about what the company calls hybrid production, which mixes live-action photography, VFX and generative tools. A second clip showed AI and VFX together producing large crowd scenes for the Netflix India title “Glory.” Lee said that under tight budgets and schedules, those scenes would normally have had to be dropped.

articles.title: Busan Market Chief Ellen Y.D. Kim Plots Year-Round ACFM 365 Platform, Warns Public Funding Has Stalled
articles.summary: The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) should grow beyond its four days in Busan into a platform that runs all year, director Ellen Y.D. Kim tells Variety. She adds that public money for the market has not grown alongside it. Kim calls the idea ACFM 365.
body: “The biggest obstacle is funding,” Kim says. “The scale and the role of the market have grown quickly, but public support has not kept pace. National funding for ACFM has stayed at the same level for two years running. The film industry is small in scale, but it is the front-runner that opens the way for other industries. Supporting film is an investment, not a subsidy, and a market needs to be understood as industry infrastructure, not as an event.”

ACFM is in its 21st edition this year. Last year, industry registration rose 14.4% and overall attendance rose 13.5%. This year there are 339 exhibiting companies and institutions from 32 countries and territories, 17% more than last year. Tech exhibitors went from seven to 18, and national agencies and film commissions from 62 to 79. Thailand, the market’s first Country of Honor, has 28 exhibitors. Japan, the ProducerHub Focus Country, has 46.

articles.title: Vietnamese Supernatural Horror ‘Bloodline: The Curse Within’ Heads to Busan Market With Mockingbird Pictures (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Vietnamese supernatural horror film “Bloodline: The Curse Within” will be introduced to international buyers by Mockingbird Pictures at the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the market of the Busan International Film Festival.
body: Award-winning actor Quách Ngọc Ngoan leads the cast. He drew acclaim for his lead turn in Victor Vu’s “The Immortal” (“Người Bất Tử”) and was most recently seen in the hit “The Journey of Heroes” (“Trại Buôn Người”). He is joined by Quang Tuấn, a familiar face in Vietnamese horror who fronts “The Corpse” franchise, and Lan Phương, who appeared in “Phi Phong: The Blood Demon,” the biggest-grossing Vietnamese horror title to date.

“The supernatural is only one half of ‘Bloodline,’” said director Đinh Đức Thiện. “What interested me was placing medicine and spirituality side by side, while exploring what people are willing to sacrifice when someone they love is threatened.”

Hoàng Gia previously led development on “The Corpse 2” (“Quỷ Nhập Tràng 2”). He said the team wanted the film to be genuinely frightening, “while grounding the horror in something deeply human – family, blood ties and the consequences passed from one generation to the next.”

Mockingbird will present the title to buyers and distributors in Busan as part of its newest lineup of Vietnamese films. Phong Duong, the company’s business director, also serves as a co-executive producer on the project.

Created by Jorge and Alberto Sánchez-Cabezudo (“Crematorium,” “The Zone”), the fact-based wild bear murder mystery that exposes the deep social conflict in the high Pyrenees marks the fourth co-production between Movistar Plus and broadcast network Arte France. articles.title: ‘Bedford Park’ Star Moon Choi Charts Her Own Path Between Korea and Hollywood
articles.summary: The rising Korean actress brings her acclaimed American indie romance with Son Sukku to Busan, where she’s also serving on the festival’s main competition jury led by Chinese filmmaking legend Zhang Yimou.
body: Indie drama Bedford Park might just prove to be Korean actress Moon Choi’s big break in the U.S. film industry — but she’s nonetheless a little apprehensive about how it will play for the fans who know her work best.

Written and directed by first-time feature filmmaker Stephanie Ahn, Bedford Park stars Choi as Audrey, a 36-year-old Brooklyn physical therapist whose mother’s car accident summons her back to the suburban New Jersey home she has never quite escaped emotionally. The other driver is Eli (rising Korean star Son Sukku of The Roundup and D.P. fame), a prickly former wrestler and Korean adoptee raised by a neglectful white mother.

When Audrey visits Eli to share insurance info, the encounter descends into a heated argument over who was responsible for the crash. Their second meeting takes a harrowing turn when Audrey suffers a miscarriage on Eli’s doorstep. Soon, a bond begins to emerge between the two, as they glimpse a kindred spirit hidden beneath each other’s self-defenses. But their intimacy is messy and hard-won, more a meeting of two wounded Asian American survivors and strivers than the typical meet-cute of Korean romances.

articles.title: Other Mommy's Strange Powers, Explained
articles.summary: The titular demon in the horror film Other Mommy is quite the strange lady indeed. Here's a breakdown of her unconventional powers and how they work.
body: One of the great benefits for horror writers and filmmakers in using a pre-established monster, creature, or antagonist is that the parameters, tropes, and power set of those characters are already understood. While creating a new entity in a horror story is of course attractive for a variety of reasons, it can be tricky in terms of selling it to a jaded audience. The lazier option is to have them conform to already well-known archetypes. The tougher option is to present them with little explanation (for extensive explanation runs the risk of turning a creepy monster into a too-familiar threat). The latter is ultimately more rewarding, but can falter if audiences get too confused.

articles.title: US country music star Ella Langley cancels show due to 'security threat'
articles.summary: Police say they checked the concert venue in Tulsa, Oklahoma but "could not find any threat".
body: US country music star Ella Langley has said she had to cancel her sold-out concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma on Friday night, due to a "serious security threat".
The singer made what she called the "incredibly difficult" decision around two hours before the show at the 19,000-seater arena was due to start.
In a post on Instagram, the 27-year-old said the threat involved "the safety of my fans, the venue staff and my team".
Cpt Richard Meulenberg from Tulsa Police Department said a person had called saying "great harm" would be done at the event with "shots fired and bombs."

articles.title: Stark warning – does new footage in Avengers: Endgame reveal the truth about Doctor Doom?
articles.summary: Warning: contains spoilers The four short scenes added to the new version has made the film the highest-grossing of all time – but the only people really enjoying this are the Disney accountants. Does it really matter which film is the highest-grossing of all time at the global box office?
body: And yet the most interesting thing about Avengers: Endgame’s return to cinemas is not how much money it has made – for the record, the rerelease, titled Avengers Endgame: Encore, had brought in another $126m worldwide by last weekend, taking its lifetime total to approximately $2.925bn (just ahead of Avatar’s $2.923bn) – but what Marvel added to the picture while we were all busy counting.

Premium-format presentations of the new version feature a new scene at the end of the film and another three during and after its credits, with some also appearing in standard screenings. The idea is presumably that these tantalising snippets will segue viewers smoothly into the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday with the sort of spring in the step that can only come from being convinced that they are now three tiny clues away from understanding the mind of Kevin Feige.

articles.title: Tenzing review – reconstruction of first summit of Everest puts Sherpa at the centre of the story
articles.summary: Genden Phuntsok brings charm and innocence to his portrayal of Tenzing Norgay, while Tom Hiddleston is suitably frank as Edmund Hillary. Here is a well intentioned, watchable, if sometimes soft-edged film with some NatGeo production values on high mountain peaks.
body: Tenzing, a former Sherpa guide whose unparalleled knowledge of the mountain and exemplary climbing skills earned him promotion to full team member, is played here by Tibetan actor Genden Phuntsok, while Hillary is robustly portrayed by Tom Hiddleston. Screenwriter Luke Davies and director Jennifer Peedom have the decent aim of restoring Tenzing’s achievement to the centre of the narrative, a tale which at the time was resoundingly claimed for Hillary and the British empire: a glorious redemption of Scott’s Antarctic ordeal 41 years earlier and a sign of divine approval for the imminent coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.

articles.title: ‘Edie Arnold Is a Loser’ Star Turned to a Video Game To Help Her Become a Punk Rock Drummer
articles.summary: Adi Madden Cabrera discusses Edie Arnold Is a Loser, playing Rock Band to become a drummer, shooting that very memorable kiss, and what's next.
body: Editor's note: The following contains spoilers for Edie Arnold Is a Loser.

Collider recently got the opportunity to chat with Cabrera about making such a splash with her first acting role and what’s been holding her back from pursuing a career in music. During the interview, she discussed the authenticity that drew her to Edie Arnold Is a Loser, her own love of music, what she did to pull off playing the drums for the movie, why one of the nuns ended up being one of her favorite characters, the best part of the entire shoot, the stand-out kiss between Edie and Walter, that fight with Kati, how the ending evolved, and what she’d like to do next with both acting and music.

COLLIDER: One of the things that I really loved about this movie is how authentic it feels. Individually, the characters feel authentic, but how they talk to each other also felt very real. Did you get a sense of that from the beginning? Was that something that was always really apparent in the script?
